title: The Goal He Didn't See
scene: You and a friend go to watch your local football team. He leaves his seat to buy drinks, misses the winning goal, and decides his absence must have brought the team luck.
sceneJa: 友人と地元のサッカーチームの試合を観戦。飲み物を買いに席を離れた友人は決勝点を見逃すが、なぜか自分が離席したおかげで勝てたと思い始める。

chunks.en: We went to watch our local football team,
chunks.ja: 地元のサッカーチームの試合を観に行った

chunks.en: neither of us had other plans.
chunks.ja: 二人ともほかに予定がなかったからだ

chunks.en: Just as the game started to get interesting,
chunks.ja: 試合がちょうど面白くなってきたころ

chunks.en: to get us something to drink.
chunks.ja: 僕らの飲み物を買いに

chunks.en: He came back a minute later,
chunks.ja: 友人は1分後に戻ってきたが
そこで初めて知ることになった
決勝点を見逃したことを

chunks.en: I tried to explain what happened,
chunks.ja: 何が起きたか説明しようとしたけれど

chunks.en: but he was more interested in
chunks.ja: 友人がもっと気にしていたのは
自分が席を外したおかげだったのかどうか

chunks.en: By the time the final whistle blew,
chunks.ja: 試合終了の笛が鳴るころには
友人はすっかり思い込んでいた

chunks.en: that leaving his seat was the reason we'd won.
chunks.ja: 自分が席を離れたから勝てたのだと

chunks.en: He offered to do it again next week,
chunks.ja: 来週もまた席を離れようかと友人は申し出た

chunks.en: that watching football was becoming a strange hobby for him.
chunks.ja: 彼にとってサッカー観戦が妙な趣味になりつつあると

questions.question: Which chunking keeps the meaning together?
options: He came back / a minute later only / to find out he'd / missed the winning goal
He came back a minute later / only to find out / he'd missed the winning goal
He came / back a minute / later only to / find out he'd missed
questions.explanation: ‘Only to find out’ is a useful unit meaning that the speaker discovered an unexpected result. Keep ‘he'd missed the winning goal’ together as what he discovered.

questions.question: What does ‘only to find out’ suggest here?
options: He returned because he already knew about the goal.
He discovered an unexpected, disappointing result after coming back.
He decided not to ask what happened.
questions.explanation: ‘Only to find out’ introduces a surprising or disappointing discovery: he had missed the decisive moment.

questions.question: Why does the speaker call football a strange hobby for his friend?
options: Because his friend is planning to leave his seat instead of watching the match.
Because his friend has forgotten the rules of football.
Because his friend refuses to buy drinks.
questions.explanation: The speaker is teasing his friend: going to a match just to miss the important moments is a rather strange way to enjoy football.

speak: Round 1: Read ‘He came back a minute later / only to find out / he'd missed the winning goal’ slowly, keeping each chunk together. Round 2: Stress ‘only’ and ‘winning goal’ to convey the surprise. Round 3: Read the whole story with playful, dry humour. Then speak for 30 seconds about a time you stepped away and missed something: What happened? How did you find out? What did you say?
review: Reuse two phrases from earlier lessons in a new situation. Lesson 76: ‘By the time ...’ (〜するころには) — here, ‘By the time the final whistle blew ...’. Lesson 78: ‘pointed out’ (指摘した) — here, ‘I pointed out that ...’. New expressions: ‘stepped away’ (少し席を離れた), ‘only to find out’ (その結果、思いがけず〜と知る), and ‘convinced himself’ (自分でそう思い込んだ).
